training_split_basis: checkpoint training set is upstream data/Hu.csv; verified when >=50% of its molecules fall in one snapshot study (released split is an upstream assumption)
reason: 6 studies / 1113 records / 12 genes share no molecule with checkpoint training or the development cohort; all are upstream-evaluation-exposed, so this is weight-independent, not fully independent
residual_exposure: Exact 19-nt antisense-core identity only; no coordinates, isoforms or near-duplicates.
Checkpoint training set is taken as upstream data/Hu.csv (the Huesken file its trainer consumes); the released split itself is an upstream assumption, recorded not assumed away.
Gene names are source strings; synonyms (e.g. 'Firefly luciferase' vs 'FireflyLuc') are not merged.

Studies upstream kept as evaluation collections (Mix/Taka) are retained at weight level. Upstream trains on Hu and selects epochs on Mix, so those molecules did not fit the weights but did steer early stopping: exposure is stronger than pure 'published eval'.
Strategy/policy selection is confined to the Huesken development cohort, so the holdout is never used to choose a winner here.
No study is free of upstream-evaluation exposure either; run --criterion fully to see it.

buildable_holdout.note: records whose accession or strands do not place exactly on a reference are excluded there, so the built cohort can be smaller than holdout_records (e.g. an accession absent from the snapshot FASTA)
